facts.text: Long ago, near the tower where Cohen and Lakra are staying, Saint Mihi fought an ancient Vraker named Kalas.
Kalas had the power to thin the veil between reality and Anahora.
Lakra believes Kalas was meddling with the same power that Brenis is trying to harness.
Wisps are otherworldly entities that inhabit the marsh and are attracted to strong, sincere emotion.
Cohen and Lakra share deeply personal memories in the marsh to attract the wisps and be guided to Kalas's lair.
Cohen tells Lakra about his family and his drowned brother, Alene.
Lakra reveals that as a child in Egypt she was married off to a grown man and endured years of abuse.
The wisps lead Cohen and Lakra to an overgrown entrance to Kalas's lair.
Inside the lair, Kalas is found fused into a mass of plant-like growth resembling the vegetation seen in Anahora and in Baroness Zanthy's castle.
A Vraker's body normally crumbles to dust after death, making Kalas's preserved fused form unusual.
Lakra suspects Kalas's unusually deep connection to Anahora is what preserved his body in plant form.
Growing within Kalas's remains is a Mandre, an extremely rare flower of Anahora.
Lakra explains that a Mandre can grow when a powerful Vraker's remains, such as ashes or teeth, stay in one place for centuries.
The Mandre is said to grant power that can help someone withstand both Brenis and Anahora itself.
Cohen and Lakra both consume the Mandre flower.
After consuming the Mandre and preparing fully, Cohen receives an invitation from Brenis proposing negotiations.
Cohen faces a choice: negotiate with Brenis, join Catalin and the Manummits to break the blockade at the mountain pass, or join Lakra to sabotage Brenis's ritual beneath Zvatra.
In the Manummit route, the rebels launch a surprise attack on an outpost while Catalin's army attacks from the other side to break the blockade of Veil Sangora.
Cohen personally turns the wheel to open the gates, breaking the blockade of Veil Sangora.
Catalin, son of the former Kenaz Scander, is revealed to be selfish, cruel, and arrogant like his father.
Craig reports that Brenis is performing a ritual using prisoners inside the castle, but Catalin dismisses this as superstition.
Cohen, Craig, Catalin, and fighters storm the castle through a secret passage beneath the mountains, the same route Catalin used to escape two years earlier when the Verkieri seized power.
Cohen and Craig find the prison cells empty, with no sign of where the prisoners were taken.
Catalin sends a group of Manummits on a suicidal assault to seize the armory despite their being too few in number.
Cohen and Craig find the desecrated corpse of Kenaz Scander sitting on the throne.
Catalin is pleased that Brenis killed his father, since it removed an obstacle to his own claim to the throne.
Brenis attacks Catalin in the throne room, and Craig sacrifices himself to protect Catalin, resulting in Craig's death.
Brenis badly wounds Catalin and then leaves, telling Cohen that his family is already waiting for him.
After defeating Zanthy's blood guard, Cohen kills the wounded Catalin himself, refusing to let him rule Veil Sangora.
Cohen finds his family seated at a table in the castle's dining hall, shrouded in crimson mist, with his youngest sister Luca missing.
Brenis says sunlight has always been his greatest weakness but claims he no longer fears it, demonstrating by passing his hand through a sunbeam.
Brenis reveals his plan to break every bone in Cohen's body, nail him to a wall, and force him to watch his family drained one by one.
Despite Brenis no longer fearing sunlight, Cohen, who arrived in human form during the day, fights and defeats him in the physical world.
Defeated, Brenis cuts open his palm to release a cloud of bloody mist that drags both himself and Cohen into Anahora.
In Anahora, Brenis transforms into a deformed monster with a flayed skull and leathery tentacles.
Cohen defeats Brenis's monstrous form within Anahora itself, something normally considered impossible.
Before vanishing into Anahora's wastelands, Brenis refuses to reveal what happened to Luca and promises he will have the last laugh.
In the epilogue, Cohen learns at a cemetery that Luca has died, but the rest of his family survived.
Cohen visits his mother Esme, who is catatonic, but she briefly regains awareness long enough to tell him she loves him.
Cohen helps his father Pieta repair the front door of their home, though conversation between them remains difficult.
Cohen announces he is leaving Veil Sangora, and Pieta gives him his blessing.
Anka prepares a lethal potion for Cohen, warning it is dangerous, intending it to be used that same night.
Anka is also leaving Veil Sangora to search for a way to remove the evil power and heal the symbols carved into her skin.
Cohen finds Luca alive in a mountain cave, transformed into a Muron rather than dead as everyone believed.
Brenis's farewell gift to Cohen was transforming Luca into a Muron instead of killing her.
The potion Anka prepared is lethal poison to both Verkieri and Moroni, and Cohen intends to use it to end Luca's suffering.
Nebaru arrives in the cave and reveals he is also a Vraker and a Dawn Walker like Cohen, working as an arbiter for the Council of Augers.
Nebaru explains there is a way to transform a Muron into a true Vrair, meaning Luca cannot become human again but need not remain a mindless monster.
Nebaru offers Cohen a purpose from the Council of Augers, saying eternity is unbearable without one.
Nebaru gives Cohen a letter with instructions and says they must leave the valley immediately before snow buries the mountain passes.
Nebaru stays behind to deal with the chaos left by Brenis and his servants, promising that in time no one will remember Brenis's name.
That same night, Cohen loads Luca into a wagon and leaves the valley.
In the Lakra route, Cohen and Lakra descend into the ruins beneath Zvatra to interrupt Brenis's ritual.
Brenis's last remaining gargoyle and soldiers guard the underground ruins, and the intrusion awakens the undead.
Inside the ritual chamber, a huge red sphere of blood churns while prisoners float around it.
Lakra destroys the blood sphere, breaking the active blood conduit through which Brenis was drawing strength from Anahora.
Brenis later explains his goal was to embrace and harness the Anacorin curse carried by the Verkieri rather than resist it.
Interrupting the ritual causes the barrier between Anahora and reality to partially collapse around Griefberg instead of closing cleanly, turning the castle into a supernatural disaster zone.
After the ritual's disruption, corpses rise, spectral entities appear, parts of the castle are torn upward, and living prisoners appear possessed by forces from Anahora.
Lakra knew disrupting the ritual carried great risk but did so believing that letting Brenis finish would cause an even larger-scale catastrophe.
Brenis was attempting to create a controlled breach into Anahora to draw power into the material world while retaining control, but Lakra's sabotage left the breach uncontrolled.
In this route, the Manummits and Catalin's forces have not yet begun their operation, leaving Cohen and Lakra to infiltrate the castle alone.
In this route, Cohen's family is found fused into Anahora's growth spreading through the castle, in a worse state than in the Manummit route.
Cohen's sister Jana begs him to run when he finds her fused into the growth.
Brenis blames Lakra for causing reality and Anahora to collide, and offers to let Cohen take his family and leave without pursuit.
Cohen refuses Brenis's offer and attacks him alongside Lakra.
During the battle, Brenis seriously wounds Lakra, but she is healed by the power of the Mandre flower she and Cohen had consumed earlier.
In the Lakra ending route, when Nebaru comes to the cave, Lakra arrives with him and reveals she works for the Council of Augers, who sent her to deal with Brenis.
In the negotiation route, after Cohen kills Brenis's three major vassals Ambress, Baker, and Zanthy and reaches maximum infamy, Brenis offers a parley at Shrikes Crag.

At the parley, Brenis brings Pater as proof that Cohen's family is alive and offers to return them and spare Lasa, including exemption from the blood tithe, in exchange for the location of the Manummit hideout.
Cohen can accept the bargain by marking the Manummit hideout entrance for Brenis, leading to its forces massacring the Manummits.
Brenis personally captures Craig during the raid on the Manummit hideout, drinking his blood and taking him away.
In the turncoat ending, Brenis honors the bargain and returns Cohen's family, and the story moves to Lasa instead of a final battle.
In the turncoat ending, Cohen never confronts Brenis in Anahora and never kills him.
In the turncoat ending, Brenis remains in power and continues extracting blood from the valley for his larger plan, while Lasa receives special privileges including permission for Christianity.
The epilogue of the turncoat ending states that Brenis's regime eventually collapses because of the arbiters, meaning Cohen's choice only delays rather than secures Brenis's rule.
In every ending route, Luca is transformed into a Muron and Nebaru eventually comes for Cohen, who enters the service of the Council of Augers.
A post-credits scene reveals Cohen survives into the modern day, still fighting supernatural forces as Anahora's corruption begins seeping into the real world again.
